root.claim: Two $n$-bit integers can be multiplied exactly on a fixed finite-tape machine in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: reduce multiplication to convolution, build two fast tape procedures whose recursion has a strict rank saving, and assemble the transforms into an exact product

motivation.text: Scanning costs a pass per transform level, giving $n\log n$; a power saving requires cheaper movement and arithmetic, then a full exact multiplication assembled around them.

children.claim: Both tape procedures arise from one fixed linear network exchanging two banks of values with frames, and recursion on it saves a power.
children.method: describe the network with frames, build a finite one with a rank deficit, then recurse

motivation.text: Each procedure must be implemented by smaller calls to itself; a network with frames lets every edge be such a call and the rank deficit makes the recursion cheaper than linear growth.

motivation.text: The recursive saving needs a concrete finite network whose rank deficit is strict, so it has to be built and its label dimensions counted.

children.claim: Calls at parameter $mf$ use $s$ calls at parameter $f$ on volume $V/W$, and $s/W<m^\tau$ with $\tau<1$ gives a power saving.
children.salient: Multiplying the parameter by $m$ raises the cost per volume by $s/W<m$, so the exponent is strictly below 1 (here $\tau=1-2^{-50}$).

children.claim: Simultaneous butterfly layers on selected coordinate bits cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, $\lambda'<1$.
children.method: apply the complex phase network, changing numerical address coordinates by packed bit additions

motivation.text: The numerical layer has the same recursive shape as the address interchange, but needs address coordinates of the arrays changed, which packed additions supply.

children.claim: Selected bits at positions $\rho+iK$ of several chunks are XORed simultaneously by packing, with a small exceptional set of addresses repaired.
The layer $H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2)$ is applied simultaneously on selected coordinate bits of complex fixed-point arrays at cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ with $\lambda'<1$.
The integer product is reduced to a convolution over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$, computed with the fast procedures, with exact recovery of the result.
children.method: chain the reductions: convolution on the ring, Gaussian resampling, chirps, Chinese-remainder axes, phase twist, then precision and cost

motivation.text: The sources present the reductions as a flow of changes of problem, each cheap, ending at a ring where the fast transforms apply; the last stage recovers the exact integer.

children.claim: Convolution over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ is computed with synthetic transforms and packed polynomial products.
children.method: apply a synthetic transform, multiply pointwise by signed packing, and apply the opposite transform

motivation.text: Over this ring the roots of unity are powers of $y$, so the transforms are cheap shifts and butterflies, and the pointwise products are ordinary integer multiplications.

children.claim: Synthetic characters cancel: sums of powers of $\omega_t$ are $t$ or $0$, so the forward and backward synthetic transforms invert each other up to $t^{-1}$.
The synthetic transform over $\mathcal R_r$ is laid out so that stored frequency order is retained through the pointwise product, with cost via simultaneous layers.
Signed packing turns polynomial products in $\mathcal R_r$ into integer products solved by the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier.
Each source Fourier transform is expressed through a transform with power-of-two axis lengths.
children.method: use Gaussian resampling in dimension $d$ with the permutations kept inside the transform

motivation.text: Power-of-two lengths are the ones the synthetic transforms handle, and keeping the permutations avoids a full sort for each.

quote.quote: so they need not be executed as separate full sorts.

children.claim: Gaussian resampling gives a source-transform identity without executing the two coordinate permutations.
Resampling lines combine over $d$ axes, with source and target permutations kept in the transform identity.
Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform, with its target permutation, into a normalized cyclic convolution; the permutation cancels.
The radix-digit coefficient list is placed on a product of pairwise coprime cyclic axes by a convolution-preserving Chinese-remainder address map.
A coefficient twist turns the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, whose negative wrap gives the cyclic wrap after untwisting.
